title: A router change is checked on broad lookups the kb answers, not only on the eval rows, so a kind expert cannot hijack a good pack
goal: A test drives kbfacts.routed over a probe set built from the kb itself (one 'What does the kb say about <article title or topic>?' question per article whose plain pack is good, plus the eval, held-out and off-kb questions) and fails naming each question that is routed while its plain pack is good on an article, so a cue or ledger rule as loose as the one BG-zpcqo7qt fixed fails at its item's landing, not at the sprint review.
notes: Retrospective of SP-7n3d4jte (2026-10-12): ST-b27c527d's checks (rag.py eval, -k pack_routes_kind on the pool's rows) passed while the gap expert routed broad lookups as 'kb lacks' (KRBTGT reset cadence, python.org Windows installers, MCP tasks capability); the worker's sweep covered only eval, held-out, off-kb and pool questions, all specific. The review found it as S1 (BG-zpcqo7qt). The test ceiling is at 100 ids: the test replaces or folds into one. Premise run 2026-10-12: 'What does the kb say about GitLab semantic versioning requirement for Catalog releases?' prints coverage none routed by kind: gap, and 'What do S1800 and S1801 say about the headless flag used by CI?' a cites file list, while the plain packs answer. Ordered after BG-hc2gficq, BG-v57estdm and BG-s4lnuekm: the test fails until the first two land. The ids are at the ceiling: fold the probe into an existing test (name it to carry router_broad_lookups); tests_ceiling.json is not touched. Planned at the 2026-10-12 draft triage (sprint 2 of 19, "Lookup correctness: router experts, the tag parser and aliases answer what the kb holds"): it serves the fitness tests of EP-gzr4mmkm: a lookup's verdict or the benchmark's measurement is wrong until it is fixed.
